$comment: Terrain volumes (docs/proposals/TERRAIN_HYDROLOGY_AND_VOLUMES.md §3 layer 2; ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3): a 3D density per cell over the height field, solid where it is above 0. A volume's `density` is a tree of nodes from a fixed vocabulary: a number (a constant); "depth" (m from the cell's centre down from the height field's surface: > 0 below it); "height" (m above sea level); {"slope": {"radius"}} (the surface's gradient over ±radius m, rise per run); {"noise": {"wavelength", "octaves", "stretchY", "stream"}} (3D gradient noise in [-1, 1], its vertical frequency stretchY times the horizontal one, 0 a 2D field); {"add" | "mul" | "min" | "max": [nodes]}; {"abs": node}; {"clamp": {"of", "min", "max"}}; {"smoothstep": {"of", "from", "to"}}. Only cells within `reach` m of the surface are evaluated; beyond it the height field stands. Cells the density adds are `material`; cells it removes become air, or water below the column's water. The prototype world type `cliffs` (generator 101) uses the volume named "cliffs"; the LOD draws the height field's top surface only.

volumes.name: cliffs
volumes.$comment: Cliffs and overhangs: on hillsides (slope 0.3 to 0.8 over ±4 m), in the part of the land a 600 m field picks, a thresholded 3D noise (40 m across, ~27 m tall) lifts the ground 14 m or sinks it 14 m with a sharp edge between: rock walls with ledges on top, leaning where the edge leans (overhangs).
